name: Ada
oneLiner: AI customer service agent platform that automates conversations across chat, messaging, email and voice.
bestFor: Brands with high support volume that want an AI agent to resolve routine questions across channels before a person steps in.

updates.text: Unified Reasoning Engine: one intelligence layer for Ada's agents across voice, chat, messaging and email; Playbooks (structured workflows) available on voice as well as chat and messaging.
Builder update: native AI generation in 60 languages, images in automated conversations, enterprise audit logging, and APIs for extending Ada.

features: One AI agent across chat, messaging, email and voice, powered by the Unified Reasoning Engine.
Playbooks: structured workflows the agent follows for multi-step requests.
APIs to connect the agent to business systems and extend it into any customer experience.
Integrations with helpdesks such as Dixa for handoff to human agents.
Channels: voice, email, chat, messenger, WhatsApp, SMS, Instagram, in-app and custom channels, all through one reasoning layer.
Integrations with Zendesk, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Genesys, Amazon Connect, Twilio Flex, Freshworks and Aircall, plus open APIs, SDKs and MCP support.
Security and compliance: SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS, CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA and AIUC-1; zero data retention with LLM providers.

pricing.text: No published prices. Ada's default model charges for every conversation the AI agent has with end users; a resolution-based model is offered to enterprises with specific needs. Pricing follows a demo call.

notes: Replaces Drift (sunset announced March 2026) in best-customer-support-software. Customer outcome figures on ada.cx are vendor-reported and not used. Third-party per-resolution prices are unsourced estimates and not used. November 2026: ada.cx/pricing shows no prices, only a form for a 30-minute call; the conversation-based model is from the pricing FAQ on ada.cx/platform. G2 shows 4.6 out of 5 (176 reviews on the main page snippet; 173-176 across snapshots).
pros: One AI agent and reasoning layer across voice, email, chat, WhatsApp, SMS and Instagram
Connects to Zendesk, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Genesys and other helpdesk and contact-center tools, with open APIs and MCP support
Security and compliance coverage including SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI DSS

cons.text: No published prices; you book a 30-minute demo call to talk pricing
Charged per conversation by default, so the bill grows with message volume
Handoff to people runs through a helpdesk you connect, such as Zendesk, Salesforce or Dixa
Built for brands with high support volume, so a smaller restaurant group may not have enough conversations to justify it

plans.billing: per conversation by default; resolution-based pricing for some enterprises
